I've been farming this land for four years now, and I know Quzhou's conditions well enough to have a clear picture of what I'm doing this season. I have 225 mu total. The wheat-maize rotation runs on the same 110 mu — winter wheat goes in October, summer maize follows right after the June wheat harvest on the same ground. That leaves 115 mu for cotton, which I keep as a cash crop to diversify income.

I'll use improved varieties for wheat (something like Shi 4185 or a local certified variety) and hybrid seed for maize — no question there. For cotton I'll go with hybrid Bt varieties to reduce bollworm pressure. My education means I actually read the agronomic guides and extension bulletins, so I calibrate fertilizer more carefully than some neighbors. I won't over-apply nitrogen on wheat — I've seen what lodging does to yield. Maize I'll push a bit harder on nitrogen since the summer heat and my well irrigation let me support it.

For irrigation: wheat needs three passes (pre-winter, jointing, heading). Maize is lower — two applications targeting tasseling and grain fill. Cotton needs four — bud stage, flowering, boll development, and one late. My well covers all of it without stress.

On tillage: after maize harvest in September, I'll do rotary tillage before wheat seeding. After wheat harvest in June, time is tight, so I direct-seed maize with no-tillage to stay on schedule. For cotton, I'll do rotary in spring to break the winter crust.

Cotton gets the most pesticide attention — five applications across the season to manage aphids, bollworm, and spider mites. Wheat and maize each get two applications (seed treatment plus one in-season fungicide/herbicide pass).
